content: Goal: rank the four frozen proposals under policy rank-2026-10-v1 using only the frozen evidence bundles. Read: four bundles (successor-anchor 6f9f3944, fine-residual-transport 442c7bd5, poincare_residual_direction adeb6448, bgcd-fine 65930410). Observations: all four bundles share the same frozen diagnostics — E5 measured train-only graph (115582 distinct edges, mean out-degree 5.4526), E6 baseline SID diagnostic same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067 (weak item-level behaviour signal), E11 geometry_operator_valid PASS, E12 behavior_dependency FAIL for the generic proxy (a positive row scalar cannot move an assignment), E13 geometry_dependency PASS, E14 CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN. So E12/E14 are common caveats and cannot separate the four; separation must be on spec completeness, numerical safeguards, sign consistency and targeting of the measured fine-layer collapse (955 L2 prefixes, 0.771 collision vs baseline 7414/0.275). Reasoning recorded: bgcd-fine is the only one with a bounded ball lift (frozen 95th-percentile residual scale), artanh clamp and a displacement clipped to half the nearest-code distance, all derived; poincare_residual_direction preserves the radius (cannot merge residuals) and derives curvature from the measured median residual norm but its behaviour signal is a tangential rotation of unquantified size plus a per-epoch temperature rescale; transport-v1 has the sign-consistent story but no bounded lift/clamp before Mobius addition and its own risk concedes a pure isometry may just permute codewords; successor-anchor's subtractive term makes codes FAR from the successor anchor cheapest, contradicting its own motivation and hypothesis, and its anchor is thinned through only 256 L1 codes. Final ranking: bgcd-fine-v1 1, poincare_residual_direction_sinkhorn_v1 2, fine-residual-behaviour-geodesic-transport-v1 3, successor-anchor-l2-poincare-sinkhorn-v1 4. Open: E14 means none of the four has its own joint path exercised, so no placement is grounded in a measured coupling, only in specification quality.

L1 untouched at baseline (E2/E3 train-only successors, E5 mean out-degree 5.4526 supports the successor table), cost matrix only inside the baseline Sinkhorn, +5-7% wall clock; it is the only one that structurally bounds the previous 955-prefix / 0.771-collision collapse instead of re-risking it, and its residual gap is only the common E12 proxy caveat and E14 unexercised path."},{"idea_id":"poincare_residual_direction_sinkhorn_v1","position":2,"reason":"Poincare cost with per-level curvature kappa_l=-1/R_l^2 derived from the measured median residual norm (E7/E9) enters the baseline Sinkhorn cost at levels 2-3 with L1 bit-identical; the tanh radial lift keeps ||p_i||<1 so E11's domain guard survives and the fixed radius means behaviour cannot merge residuals onto one fine code, the direct structural answer to the 955 prefixes / 0.771 collision; placed second, not first, because the behaviour enters only as a tangential rotation whose magnitude is unquantified while E6 shows the item-level prefix-behaviour signal is weak (0.0907 vs 0.067 null), and the per-epoch eps_l rescale risks a near-hard plan (its own risk 3)."},{"idea_id":"fine-residual-behaviour-geodesic-transport-v1","position":3,"reason":"Cheapest and most sign-consistent coupling (item transported along its transition direction so the L2 token names where the item leads), L1 byte-identical, constants derived from batch statistics (median residual norm rho_l, mean behaviour strength sbar) and an explicit Euclidean comparison (E10); placed third because the Mobius sum is applied to the unlifted residual r with no ball-norm clamp (E11's domain guard was validated only on a test vector, and the proposal's own risk list flags boundary blow-up), the transport length reaches a full median residual norm so many L2 assignments move at once, and its own risk concedes an isometry may merely permute codewords — unseparable in one run against E6's weak 0.0907-vs-0.067 signal."},{"idea_id":"successor-anchor-l2-poincare-sinkhorn-v1","position":4,"reason":"The equation contradicts the claimed mechanism: C2 = d2_r/a_i - beta_i*d2_b/m_i makes the cost lowest for codes FAR from the successor anchor b_i, so the assigned L2 token encodes where the item does not lead, against its own motivation and hypothesis (i) that MI(level-2 code; successor coarse group) rises; the anchor is also averaged through only the 256 L1 code embeddings, thinning exactly the behaviour signal E6 already measures as near-null (0.0907 vs 0.067), it leaves L3 at baseline, and it gives no ball lift or clamp (E7/E9), leaving only the common E12/E14 caveats as support."}],"objection":"Every placement is grounded in specification quality, not in measured coupling: the four bundles share the same frozen diagnostics, E11 (geometry operator valid) and E13 (geometry dependency) PASS but E12 behavior_dependency FAILs for the generic proxy and E14 reports the candidate joint path not run, so none of the four has demonstrated that training-only behaviour actually moves an assignment inside the baseline Sinkhorn plan; the 955-prefix / 7414-prefix / 0.771-collision figures that all four motivations rest on

appear in the proposals, not as an OBSERVED bundle entry, and E5's coverage is over sampled users with hub-heavy degree structure, so the ranking is an ordering of how safely each design could be implemented and refuted in the single frozen run, and could be overturned by the one Stage 3 test_recall@10 measurement."}
